intro.title: Research behind observations
paragraphs: This research library investigates the ideas behind specific event descriptions, emotional language and communication. It restores the scope of the earlier nvc-app guide while separating measured findings from interpretation and practical suggestions.

Evidence about related methods is not proof that this app or the full NVC-informed sequence improves clinical outcomes. The historical sources and outstanding fact-check questions are preserved separately for continuing review.

sections.title: Observation methods
sections.description: What professional behavioral observation actually records.

content.text: An observation is a record of an event from a particular perspective. Research methods distinguish a description of an action from a hypothesis about its meaning. That distinction is useful for organizing a story; it does not decide whether anyone's feelings or interpretation are legitimate.

content.title: How direct observation is defined
content.method: Clinical-practice review of school-based observation methods, including defining target behaviors and recording context.
content.result: The authors describe procedures for identifying behaviors, gathering contextual information, recording observations, and synthesizing results for clinical practice.
content.meaning: Time, setting, words, and actions can make a record easier to inspect or compare.
content.limits: This was not an outcome trial of NVC, journaling, or this application's checklist.

content.text: For personal writing, names, quotations, counts and times are optional when available. Exact measurements belong to formal recording protocols, not a threshold for whether someone should be believed.

sections.title: Language, memory & self-talk
sections.description: What research finds about concrete words and ways of thinking.

content.title: Concrete and abstract words in memory
content.method: Two laboratory experiments tested recall and recognition of words presented alone or in differing sentence contexts.
content.result: Participants generally recalled and recognized concrete words better than abstract words; adding sentence context did not eliminate that pattern.
content.meaning: The word-concreteness effect offers a reason to study specificity, not a universal instruction to remove abstractions.
content.limits: Words in experimental memory lists are not the same as descriptions of emotionally important events.

content.title: Practicing concrete thinking
content.method: Experimental proof-of-principle work examined repeated concrete-thinking exercises among people with dysphoria.
content.result: The researchers reported reduced dysphoria after concreteness training in this research program.
content.meaning: Specific ways of processing experiences may matter psychologically; the full original 'Why try this?' area was pointing toward this literature.
content.limits: Training involved a defined cognitive exercise. Simply adding time or place to an Observation is not equivalent treatment.

content.title: Inner speech is more than a single voice
content.method: An integrative review examined developmental, cognitive, and neurobiological approaches to internal speech.
content.result: Inner speech has several proposed cognitive functions and varies among people; the scientific picture is not a single settled mechanism.
content.meaning: The words we use for our experiences may matter for self-reflection, but do not all work alike.
content.limits: The review does not show that this app changes self-talk, behavior, or symptoms.

sections.title: Feelings & affect labeling
sections.description: Emotion-labeling findings—and why they are not observation findings.

content.title: Putting feelings into words
content.method: An fMRI experiment compared labeling emotional images with other encoding tasks.
content.result: Labeling negative emotional stimuli was associated with lower amygdala responses and greater right ventrolateral prefrontal activity in the laboratory task.
content.meaning: This is relevant to a possible next step of identifying feelings; it is not evidence for removing feelings from an observation.
content.limits: Brain-activity differences are not themselves evidence of clinical effectiveness or that this specific writing step produces the same effect.

content.text: The allneeds pathway separates Observation and Feeling as tools for exploration. That sequence is a design hypothesis informed by NVC, not a clinically proven causal chain.

sections.title: Communication & interpretation
sections.description: How language, expectations, and inferred intent relate to interaction.

content.title: Subtle wording and judgments of blame
content.method: Experimental studies tested whether linguistic framing influences how people assign responsibility.
content.result: Changes in phrasing affected judgments of blame and financial liability in the study context.
content.meaning: The way events are described may shape listeners' inferences. It is worth making specific details available alongside conclusions.
content.limits: Framing effects do not tell us which account is truthful or establish that a neutral-sounding sentence is the best response.

content.title: I-language and communicating perspective
content.method: Participants rated hypothetical opening statements for conflict discussions with different pronouns and perspectives.
content.result: Statements using I-language and communicating both perspectives were rated as less hostile than alternatives.
content.meaning: There is evidence that an opening statement's style can influence perceived hostility.
content.limits: These were ratings of hypothetical discussions, not measured reductions in real-world relationship conflict.

content.title: Appraisals during recurring conflict discussions
content.method: 77 recently married couples took part in four observed conflict conversations; appraisals were recorded before each conversation.
content.result: Changes in expectations and attributions predicted within-person changes in communication, especially expectations about being understood.
content.meaning: An interpretation and an observable event are distinct but both can matter for understanding communication.
content.limits: Associations from a married-couple sample do not prove changing the observation sentence causes a better interaction.

content.title: Hostile-attribution research
content.method: Researchers examined how hostile-attribution bias and emotional responding related to forms of adult aggression.
content.result: The research investigated relationships between how ambiguous acts were interpreted, negative emotions, and aggressive behavior.
content.meaning: It provides context for considering uncertainty when writing about someone's intentions.
content.limits: It is not a method for discounting reports of mistreatment or determining whether an attribution was justified.

content.html: Both can stay. “She ended the call while I was speaking” describes an event. “I felt dismissed and wondered if it was deliberate” preserves the experience and interpretation.

sections.title: Measurement & reliability
sections.description: What systematic reviews and recording research show about rigor.

content.title: What researchers report checking
content.method: A survey examined 596 experimental articles from two behavior-analysis journals (2017–2021).
content.result: 96.4% reported interobserver agreement for participant behavior; 54.7% reported procedural fidelity and, among those reporting fidelity, 17.7% also reported agreement on fidelity.
content.meaning: Rigor requires inspecting how observations are recorded and how consistently procedures are followed.
content.limits: Reporting rates are not measures of accuracy, nor validation of a personal journal or allneeds.

content.title: Are assessments reliable and valid?
content.method: A systematic review identified 46 studies reporting reliability or validity for six criterion-referenced ABA assessments.
content.result: The evidence gave conflicting support; the authors highlighted measurement terminology and methodological limitations.
content.meaning: Even established observational assessments need direct validation rather than assuming that observable wording ensures scientific reliability.
content.limits: These six tools are not the allneeds Observation tool.

content.title: ABC recording as a method
content.method: An educational methods resource describes recording antecedents, a specified behavior, and what followed.
content.result: ABC notes can organize repeated event data and help investigators examine recurring patterns.
content.meaning: Optional counts, duration, latency and context can be useful in systematic observations.
content.limits: This resource explains a recording procedure; a single ABC record does not establish causation, intention, or clinical benefit.

content.text: A personal observation does not require interobserver agreement, a standardized instrument, or exact measurement. These concepts explain what formal measurement rigor involves, not a standard that users must meet.

sections.title: Needs & social connection
sections.description: What the broader psychology establishes—and what is only an analogy.

content.title: Autonomy, competence and relatedness
content.method: An integrative theoretical and empirical review summarizes Self-Determination Theory and another personality-systems framework.
content.result: The review discusses autonomy, competence and relatedness in human motivation, development and wellbeing.
content.meaning: Studying motivations and needs is reasonable; the site's Need vocabulary can be compared with such constructs.
content.limits: SDT's three needs are not a validation of all NVC or allneeds Need labels, or proof that observation writing satisfies them.

content.title: Evidence about human connection
content.method: The U.S. Surgeon General's 2023 advisory synthesizes public-health evidence about social connection.
content.result: The advisory documents meaningful associations between social connection and health across populations.
content.meaning: Connection is an important topic to consider when describing interpersonal events and possible needs.
content.limits: Public-health evidence about relationships does not establish that an observation sentence improves connection.

content.text: The link from an event to a Feeling, Need or Strategy is a reflective prompt. The research above supplies context for those subjects; it does not show that software can infer a particular person's Needs from wording.

sections.title: Recall, certainty & limitations
sections.description: When a record is helpful, and when it cannot settle a dispute.

content.title: Memory and later information
content.method: A systematic review examined nine studies on cognitive abilities and misinformation susceptibility in eyewitness tasks.
content.result: The review found varied evidence about susceptibility; stronger cognitive ability did not eliminate the possibility of misinformation effects.
content.meaning: It helps explain why timestamps, contemporaneous notes and marked uncertainty may be valuable when precision matters.
content.limits: Eyewitness tasks do not validate this app as a credibility checker, and memory uncertainty does not negate a person's experience.

items: Someone's intent is not directly measurable from a written description alone.
Details added after an event can be approximate. Mark uncertainty rather than inventing precision.
Different observers can encounter different parts of a situation. Context and cultural or linguistic conventions affect interpretations.
The detector only matches local word patterns. A green Quick Check result is not a research-based truth, reliability, or completeness score.
Nothing here is a diagnosis, legal standard, clinical assessment or replacement for professional care.

sections.title: Practice & examples
sections.description: Turn broad wording into an event description without deleting meaning.

items.observation: “During our conversation on Tuesday, I finished two sentences after you began speaking.”
items.why: This names one event. A person can still explain that they felt unheard.

items.observation: “The meeting invitation listed everyone on my team except me. I wondered whether that was intentional.”
items.why: The omission and the interpretation are recorded separately; neither is erased.

items.observation: “When I asked a question, he said, ‘Read the email,’ and ended the conversation.”
items.why: The quotation is usable detail. It does not require withdrawing the judgment about rudeness.

items.observation: “She recorded 62 work hours over the previous seven days.”
items.why: The count describes the schedule; whether it is excessive remains a meaningful appraisal.

content.text: These are examples of a writing convention, not outputs of a validated clinical intervention. You may choose to leave a personal journal entry in your own words.

sections.title: Source library
sections.description: Full references and claim-specific limitations in one place.

content.text: Sources are ordered by their first appearance in this guide. Each link opens a publication record or official resource. Some findings are experimental, others correlational, integrative, methodological, or public-health guidance. None directly validates the allneeds Observation tool.

sources.title: Direct behavioral observation in school settings: Bringing science to practice
sources.fit: School-based observational coding, definitions, context, and reporting; not a study of this app.

sources.title: Mechanisms of word concreteness effects in explicit memory: Does context availability play a role?
sources.fit: Concrete versus abstract words in laboratory recall and recognition, not personal event narratives.

sources.title: Concreteness training reduces dysphoria: Proof-of-principle for repeated cognitive bias modification in depression
sources.fit: Repeated concrete-thinking training for dysphoric participants, not NVC observation writing.

sources.title: Inner speech: Development, cognitive functions, phenomenology, and neurobiology
sources.fit: Reviews what is known and uncertain about inner speech; no observation-checklist intervention.

sources.title: Putting feelings into words: Affect labeling disrupts amygdala activity in response to affective stimuli
sources.fit: Emotion labeling in a laboratory image task, not writing neutral observations or clinical outcomes.

sources.title: Subtle linguistic cues influence perceived blame and financial liability
sources.fit: Linguistic framing of events affected blame judgments in experiments, not the efficacy of avoiding evaluations.

sources.title: I understand you feel that way, but I feel this way: The benefits of I-language and communicating perspective during conflict
sources.fit: Participants rated likely hostility and defensiveness to hypothetical conflict openers; actual conflict outcomes not measured.

sources.title: Communication during marital conflict: When couples alter their appraisal, they change their behavior
sources.fit: 77 married couples across four conversations; observed association, not randomized NVC treatment.

sources.title: Hostile attributional bias, negative emotional responding, and aggression in adults: Moderating effects of gender and impulsivity
sources.fit: Attributional bias and aggression associations, not proof that a user's account is inaccurate.

sources.title: Interobserver agreement and procedural fidelity: An odd asymmetry
sources.fit: How researchers report agreement and intervention fidelity; does not measure this site's reliability.

sources.title: Validity and reliability evidence for assessments based in applied behavior analysis: A systematic review
sources.fit: Six established ABA assessments, not validity of allneeds Observation or a personal journal.

sources.title: Descriptive assessments and ABC recording
sources.fit: Explains antecedent-behavior-consequence data collection; practice resource, not original experimental evidence.

sources.title: Becoming who you are: An integrative review of self-determination theory and personality systems interactions theory
sources.fit: Context for autonomy, competence and relatedness; does not validate allneeds' wider NVC-inspired Need list.

sources.authors: U.S. Office of the Surgeon General
sources.title: Our epidemic of loneliness and isolation: The healing effects of social connection and community
sources.fit: Public health and relationships; not evidence that writing observations improves connection.

sources.title: Do cognitive abilities reduce eyewitness susceptibility to the misinformation effect? A systematic review
sources.fit: Eyewitness misinformation paradigms, not an accuracy or credibility test for personal narratives.
